documents.summary: Tier 1. Course syllabus for UC Davis's computer architecture course (Prof. Jason Lowe-Power), with a section on generative AI tools. It encourages students to use GitHub Copilot and ChatGPT when appropriate, lists acceptable uses (code help, drafting from one's own inputs, grammar) and one unacceptable use (unedited AI-written text), and holds students responsible for reviewing all submitted code and text.

excerpts.text: I encourage you to use these tools when appropriate.
Using GitHub Copilot to help you write code.
Using ChatGPT to help improve grammar in your writing.
Using ChatGPT to write text for you without editing or reviewing it.
You should always review the output of these tools before submitting it.
You are responsible for all of the code and text you submit.
please ask me to clarify before submitting work using these tools.

documents.title: Fall 2024 syllabus template
documents.summary: Tier 3. Memo from the CLAS associate deans to department heads and faculty of the college that houses Iowa's Department of Computer Science, announcing the revised Fall 2024 collegiate syllabus template. Its AI section asks instructors to state permissible AI uses and integrity expectations, keep discussing AI policies through the semester, and teach students how to cite AI use; department heads must review all syllabi for compliance. The AI guidance points to the Provost's 'AI in the Classroom' page.
